title: Kubernetes Essentials
description: Pods, deployments, services and kubectl for running containers at scale

questions.question: What is the smallest deployable unit in Kubernetes?
questions.explanation: A Pod wraps one or more containers that share networking and storage. Kubernetes schedules Pods, not individual containers.

questions.question: Which object keeps a set number of Pod replicas running and handles rolling updates?
questions.explanation: A Deployment manages ReplicaSets to keep the desired number of Pods running, and rolls out new versions gradually.

questions.question: Which object gives a stable network endpoint to a changing set of Pods?
questions.explanation: A Service selects Pods by label and provides a stable virtual IP and DNS name, load-balancing across them.

questions.question: Which command-line tool is used to interact with a Kubernetes cluster?
questions.explanation: kubectl talks to the API server to create, inspect and delete resources. kubeadm bootstraps clusters and helm manages charts.

questions.question: Which control plane component stores all cluster state as key-value data?
questions.explanation: etcd is the consistent key-value store behind the API server. Backing it up is backing up the cluster's state.

questions.question: Which object ensures one copy of a Pod runs on every (or every matching) node?
questions.explanation: DaemonSets suit node-level agents such as log collectors and monitoring exporters.

questions.question: Which agent runs on each node and makes sure the containers in its Pods are running?
questions.explanation: The kubelet receives Pod specs for its node and works with the container runtime to start and monitor containers.

questions.question: Which object should hold sensitive values such as passwords and API tokens?
questions.explanation: Secrets are meant for sensitive data. Note they are only base64-encoded by default, so enable encryption at rest and restrict access with RBAC.

questions.question: What does a failing readiness probe cause?
choices: The Pod is removed from Service endpoints
questions.explanation: A failing readiness probe stops traffic to the Pod without restarting it. A failing liveness probe restarts the container.

questions.question: Which workload object is designed for stateful apps that need stable network identities and persistent storage per replica?
questions.explanation: StatefulSets give each Pod a stable name (such as db-0, db-1) and its own PersistentVolumeClaim, and start them in order.
